 Korean Stunt Actress, 25, Dies In Car Accident; Death Only Comes To Light 2 Months Later When K-Dramas Pay Tribute
 Stuntwoman Kim Hyun Yi, who had doubled for stars like Ha Ji Won, was honoured with a tribute in Doctor X: Mafia In White.

 A South Korean stuntwoman who had doubled for actresses Ha Ji Won and Lee Si Young , has died in a car accident while on her way to filming. She was just 25.
 Kim Hyun Yi died in August this year, but news of her passing only came to light two months later, after two K-dramas she had worked on paid tribute to her in their premiere episodes earlier this month.
 The first episode of Doctor X: Mafia In White on Oct 9 ended with a tribute that read: "We mourn our precious colleague, the late Kim Hyun Yi, who ran alongside us."
 The next day, 100 Days Of Deception also honoured her with a message: "We will never forget stunt actress Kim Hyun Yi."
 The unexpected tributes left viewers wondering who she was, with news of her death subsequently making headlines.
 Before becoming a stunt actress, Hyun Yi was a member of South Korea's national taekwondo demonstration team and had travelled around the world promoting the martial art.
 She later worked as a taekwondo instructor before discovering stunt work during a performance and deciding to pursue it professionally.
 Her credits included hit K-drama The Penthouse and horror film Dark Nuns , which starred Song Hye Kyo .
 Park Ji Hye, leader of stunt team Mongdol Action, who had worked with Hyun Yi, became emotional while remembering her late colleague.
 She described Hyun Yi as one of the industry's top female stunt performers, praising her professionalism, ability to work with actors and dedication to maintaining her physique.
 In an unfortunate twist, another actress named Kim Hyun Yi found herself caught up in the tragedy.
 The theatre actress, who shares the same name as the late stuntwoman, discovered that her photos were being circulated online and used in reports about Hyun Yi's death.
 On Oct 14, she took to social media to clarify that she was very much alive.
 "I am a completely different person from the deceased," she wrote, adding that the mix-up had caused her serious emotional distress.
 She urged netizens to stop sharing the incorrect information and asked anyone who came across posts featuring her photos to alert her via direct message.
 The tribute in Doctor X that brought news of Hyun Yi's passing to light.
 She was also was remembered by the 100 Days of Deception production team.
